terminal_target_provenance.rule: TARGET vs TRAJECTORY, recorded separately: the terminal touch state is ANCHORED to the v3 gate3 seed (a physics-verified pose: registration anchor + terminal alignment both aim at it), so the acceptance criteria are decided by that seed, NOT by HaMeR. The HaMeR streams shape the trajectory only; their occlusion-phase accuracy (left conf 0.52-0.68 on the grasp window, smoke 6's documented P1 limitation) therefore degrades trajectory fidelity without touching the terminal criterion.

table_clearance_clamp.strategy: explicit z lower-bound clamp: raise the base-z command by the per-frame deficit so the lowest hand collision geom clears the table by >= 60 mm; disclosed substitute for the unusable MANO depth axis

base_y_corridor_world_centring.rule: the finding-3 corridor restored to world-frame semantics: world palm y within +-0.05 m of the box centreline under the moved mounts (v25 right -0.095 / left +0.035 m); the r5-era slide-y clamp assumed mount origin y=0

approach_height_budget.why: r8 ticket item 3: the 30 mm clearance sat below the mounted hand's z tracking deficit; every generation grazed the table early-clip (r5n/r6/r7 right [5-18], left [32, 243-265])

right.rule: command clamp to [jlo+|forcerange|/kp, jhi-|forcerange|/kp] on joints whose seed terminal value lies inside the band; exempt joints keep the r7 stream (their excess is the winding rule's own part-1 allowance)

left.rule: command clamp to [jlo+|forcerange|/kp, jhi-|forcerange|/kp] on joints whose seed terminal value lies inside the band; exempt joints keep the r7 stream (their excess is the winding rule's own part-1 allowance)

smoothing.why: HaMeR frames are independent per-frame estimates (uncorrelated jitter); 15 frames = 0.50 s at 30 fps averages that out while staying at least 2x shorter than the task's own timescales (approach ~12 frames, lift ~7 frames). The constrained solve's signed rate band is the second, command-side low-pass.

right.unreachable_note: a DoF counted here holds a tracking error above the tolerance at the first commanded pose, which on this scene is sustained box contact: a finger in contact holds a contact-deflection error rather than the commanded value, and a wrist slide on the list means the commanded descent itself is outside the floating wrist's reachable set -- no approach path reaches it. The ramp caps the *command* rate; it cannot make an unreachable pose reachable. On this run every wrist DoF delivered the commanded pose; the shortfall is on the finger joints only.
right.wrist_reachable_note: per-DoF reachability, dual-hand scene: on the superseded single-hand scene the finding was the opposite -- the palm rested on the box top and the commanded wrist descent was unreachable outright. Kept as a recorded finding so the change of scene is visible rather than silent.

rate_caps.source: free-space step/ramp measurement of this model's own servos (hinges 1.5 rad/s, wrist_y 0.2 m/s), tightened per axis to the servo's own derived winding allowance where the W6a re-scale put that below the measurement (x/z: 45 N / 280 = 0.1607 m/s); recorded in rerun_evidence.velocity_gate.floating_wrist_servo_ceiling

servo_winding_rate.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per wrist hinge: (1) realised rate <= |forcerange|/dof_damping, (2) at most 3 consecutive control intervals above that same cap, (3) every interval in which the servo outran the command-side trackable rate 2.0 rad/s has its excess over the commanded rate explained as this DoF's own wind-up release (release_j(t) = sqrt(kp_j * windup_j(t)^2 / (dof_M0_j + armature_j)), windup_j(t) = ctrl_j(t) - qpos_j(t)) with the actuator off its force limit. kv = 0 does not weaken the bound: dof_damping = 1.2 is what makes a finite bound exist at all. The bound is tight -- the free-space step asymptote of this servo plateaus at 4.90-4.97 rad/s (both directions, both step signs), within 2% of it; with dof_damping forced to 0 the plateau disappears entirely.

dv <= a_max * tau_s.rejected_because: an order of magnitude above the measured transient: forcerange/I ~ 94-98 rad/s^2 is the acceleration ceiling of a kp=14, I~0.062 wrist hinge, and tau_s = 0.2857 s is a window the command rate gives, not the servo.  A bound an order of magnitude above every achievable value gates nothing.

servo_winding_position.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per finger joint: (1) excess beyond jnt_range <= |forcerange|/kp, (2) at most 3 consecutive control frames (150 ms at 20 Hz), (3) the transient is elastic wind-up: there is a contact torque on that DoF, the actuator is not on its force limit while it happens, and kp*(ctrl-qpos) accounts for the whole non-actuator load on the DoF to 5%. An excursion during saturation is never exempted, and neither is one on a freely drifting joint.

servo_winding_rate_hinge.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per wrist hinge: (1) realised rate <= |forcerange|/dof_damping, (2) at most 3 consecutive control intervals above that same cap, (3) every interval in which the servo outran the command-side trackable rate 2.0 rad/s has its excess over the commanded rate explained as this DoF's own wind-up release (release_j(t) = sqrt(kp_j * windup_j(t)^2 / (dof_M0_j + armature_j)), windup_j(t) = ctrl_j(t) - qpos_j(t)) with the actuator off its force limit. kv = 0 does not weaken the bound: dof_damping = 1.2 is what makes a finite bound exist at all. The bound is tight -- the free-space step asymptote of this servo plateaus at 4.90-4.97 rad/s (both directions, both step signs), within 2% of it; with dof_damping forced to 0 the plateau disappears entirely.

dv <= a_max * tau_s.rejected_because: an order of magnitude above the measured transient: forcerange/I ~ 94-98 rad/s^2 is the acceleration ceiling of a kp=14, I~0.062 wrist hinge, and tau_s = 0.2857 s is a window the command rate gives, not the servo. registered.definition: anatomical registration (Main Front B): constant grasp-window offset between the solved palm path and the retargeted input's palm target measured and subtracted; registered = ||dev - bias|| per frame. Raw legs above are kept unhidden. NOTE: the raw legs are robot-internal (solve vs retargeted input; executed vs commanded) -- no MANO wrist series enters them, so this calibration is the tool-frame bias of the input construction, not a palm-plate-vs-MANO-wrist offset
registered.method: grasp-window mean of the per-frame palm deviation vector (solve minus retargeted input), subtracted before scoring

pass_basis: Front B2 priority inversion: the palm leg is scored on the REGISTERED (bias-subtracted) task-space deviation and the raw palm number stays above; the fingertip-vs-MANO criterion is DROPPED (the curl adapts by contact at the terminal seed blend -- deviation from the MANO fingertip pattern is reported under constrained_solve_fingertip_max_m, not scored). The executed-vs-commanded tracking leg is unchanged

servo_winding_position.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per finger joint: (1) excess beyond jnt_range <= |forcerange|/kp, (2) at most 3 consecutive control frames (150 ms at 20 Hz), (3) the transient is elastic wind-up: there is a contact torque on that DoF, the actuator is not on its force limit while it happens, and kp*(ctrl-qpos) accounts for the whole non-actuator load on the DoF to 5%. An excursion during saturation is never exempted, and neither is one on a freely drifting joint.

servo_winding_rate_hinge.rule: three-part servo winding tolerance, per wrist hinge: (1) realised rate <= |forcerange|/dof_damping, (2) at most 3 consecutive control intervals above that same cap, (3) every interval in which the servo outran the command-side trackable rate 2.0 rad/s has its excess over the commanded rate explained as this DoF's own wind-up release (release_j(t) = sqrt(kp_j * windup_j(t)^2 / (dof_M0_j + armature_j)), windup_j(t) = ctrl_j(t) - qpos_j(t)) with the actuator off its force limit. kv = 0 does not weaken the bound: dof_damping = 1.2 is what makes a finite bound exist at all. The bound is tight -- the free-space step asymptote of this servo plateaus at 4.90-4.97 rad/s (both directions, both step signs), within 2% of it; with dof_damping forced to 0 the plateau disappears entirely.

dv <= a_max * tau_s.rejected_because: an order of magnitude above the measured transient: forcerange/I ~ 94-98 rad/s^2 is the acceleration ceiling of a kp=14, I~0.062 wrist hinge, and tau_s = 0.2857 s is a window the command rate gives, not the servo.  A bound an order of magnitude above every achievable value gates nothing.

registered.definition: anatomical registration (Main Front B): constant grasp-window offset between the solved palm path and the retargeted input's palm target measured and subtracted; registered = ||dev - bias|| per frame. Raw legs above are kept unhidden. NOTE: the raw legs are robot-internal (solve vs retargeted input; executed vs commanded) -- no MANO wrist series enters them, so this calibration is the tool-frame bias of the input construction, not a palm-plate-vs-MANO-wrist offset
registered.method: grasp-window mean of the per-frame palm deviation vector (solve minus retargeted input), subtracted before scoring

pass_basis: Front B2 priority inversion: the palm leg is scored on the REGISTERED (bias-subtracted) task-space deviation and the raw palm number stays above; the fingertip-vs-MANO criterion is DROPPED (the curl adapts by contact at the terminal seed blend -- deviation from the MANO fingertip pattern is reported under constrained_solve_fingertip_max_m, not scored). The executed-vs-commanded tracking leg is unchanged

trajectory_error.metric_definition_caveat: the reference curve is the HAND BOUNDING-BOX centre (the only per-frame pixel signal in the npz), not the wrist landmark: the box centre moves OPPOSITE to the wrist when fingers curl (an articulation lever), so this metric is an UPPER BOUND on true wrist tracking error. The round-4b tradeoff sweep (SG windows 5/9/15/21/31 frames) moves it by <2% of the span (0.329/0.201 -> 0.320/0.193) -- the residual is SYSTEMATIC, not jitter, and no filter setting can close it. A wrist-landmark pixel reference (MediaPipe wrist) is the fix and is perception scope.

smoothness_comparison.metric: mean |second difference| of the realised wrist joints (6 slides+hinges) per control second, over the video grid; frozen before this run

r101_comparison.purpose: generation comparison: r10 (pre-stops, r10 fixture 180cd84ee195..., nq/nu 65/50) vs r10.1 (this run, r10 fixture + yaw registration stops 899183df2dd0..., nq/nu 65/50). r7->r8 is the W6b execution round: four ctrl-layer fixes -- (1) the base-y corridor restored to world-frame semantics per mount (intersect-or-nearest, disclosed), (2) the F6 right corridor aim subsumed by (1), (3) the approach-height budget (clamp clearance 30 -> 60 mm), (4) a holdable-band finger command clamp (2x |forcerange|/kp on joints whose seed terminal lies inside the band). Criteria, gates and the frozen retarget stream are unchanged; every difference below is execution-layer physics. A command-side slide-rate cap at the winding gate physical bound was TRIED and REVERTED: re-solving under it reshaped the approach (the right start swung over the box top edge) and the box was knocked over during settle, losing gate2 -- the rate_slide amplitude residual (+5% over the physical bound) is the accepted cost.

r101_comparison.generation_read: The r6 name-addressing inheritance is confirmed: the v25 re-run needed ZERO layout migration fixes (the only code touch was reading the follower's shoulder anchor off the model's arm_yaw body, the v22 env pattern, for the moved mounts r-95/l+35). The kinematic layer is bit-stable: gate1's command terminal is identical to the micro-metre (seed-anchored), constrained-solve records agree with r6 to ~1e-9, and the wrist-referenced criterion of record moved -0.22 mm (right) / +5 um (left). The whole executed trajectory translated with its mount; gate2 contact evidence is unchanged (35->37 / 39->40 frames); gate3 support frames 12->12 / 23->25. Only two execution magnitudes moved >20 percent (gate4 right over-range, gate5 left execution deviation), both carried FAILs -- no gate boolean flipped. The retarget stream needs no re-tuning for the v25 engage configuration.
